explanation: Both captures are the same browser, the same width, and a page that has been settled: reduced motion, animations and transitions finished or stopped, fonts and images loaded. The same drawing twice is the same picture, so the allowed difference is zero pixels. pixelmatch's per-pixel threshold is 0, which counts any channel change. A tolerance for anti-aliasing is not used, because both sides are drawn by that same browser. One differing pixel fails unless that page, width, and browser is in the accepted-differences register.
